title: Zelenskyy asked Trump to sanction Russian and Chinese companies over Starlink rival - The New Voice of Ukraine
body: Zelenskyy Calls on Trump to Impose Sanctions on Companies Involved in Rassvet Satellite Network / The New Voice of Ukraine Exclusive Nation business life opinion Russian war Nation Zelenskyy asked Trump to sanction Russian and Chinese companies over Starlink rival 3 October, 06:58 PM World Read NV on Google Volodymyr Zelenskyy called on Donald Trump to impose sanctions against Russian and Chinese companies (Photo: REUTERS/CAITLIN OCHS) President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has called on his American counterpart, Donald Trump, to impose sanctions on Russian and Chinese companies involved in building the Rassvet satellite network, a potential rival to Starlink, in an interview with the Financial Times on Oct. 3. Russia accelerated work on its own satellite network with Chinese support after Russian forces began using SpaceX's Starlink for military purposes, Zelenskyy said. "We know that China is working on satellites, working on the ability to help Russia create an analog of Starlink," Zelenskyy said. He said Rassvet could become operational "by the end of this year or early next year." Ad According to Zelenskyy, he has asked Trump several times to impose sanctions on organizations involved in building this system. The most recent time this was raised, he said, was during his meeting with Trump in New York on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly. Read also: Ukraine urges U.S. sanctions on firms behind Russia’s Rassvet satellite network On Oct. 1, Denys Senyk, deputy head of the Ukrainian embassy mission in Washington, said Ukraine is asking the United States to impose sanctions on a number of Russian companies and individuals involved in building the Rassvet satellite network. What is known about the Rassvet satellite system On July 20, the Russian company Bureau 1440 put a second group of satellites into orbit for the Rassvet network. Presidential adviser Serhii "Flash" Beskrestnov said Russia carried out both launches — in March and in July — from the Plesetsk cosmodrome. In theory, these satellites could also be launched from the Baikonur and Vostochny cosmodromes. According to Flash, one Soyuz-2.1b carrier rocket puts 20 satellites into orbit. He estimates Russia will need 12 to 15 such launches to build its basic constellation. All components of the Soyuz-2.1b, except the engines, are made by the Progress enterprise, which Ukraine has struck with Flamingo missiles. In Beskrestnov's view, Russia's own satellite network could pose a serious threat to Ukraine. Read also: Russia's Starlink satellite rival fails to reach orbit again Satellite communications expert Volodymyr Stepanets told defense outlet Militarnyi on Aug. 1 that Rassvet satellites provide "communication windows" over Ukraine. There are at least two such windows a day, each lasting more than an hour. The military war may be swinging in our favor, but the information war continues.
